comparisons.peer_topic: Redemption Rights and Depositary Share Structures
comparisons.peer_summary: The Corporation may redeem most preferred stock series at its option at liquidation preference plus unpaid dividends, except for Series B and Series L which lack early redemption rights. Ownership is generally held via depositary shares representing fractional interests in preferred stock, with dividend payment frequencies and minimum rates varying by series as detailed in the table footnotes.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Bank of America disclose that certain preferred stock series are issued as depositary shares representing fractional interests in the underlying preferred stock. However, the fractional interest ratios differ: Citi's Series DD depositary shares represent a 1/25th interest (c_2024_8_P617_S001), while Bank of America's disclosures note depositary shares representing either a 1/25th, 1/1000th, or 1/1200th interest depending on the specific series (bac_2024_8_P393_S001, bac_2024_8_P390_S001, bac_2024_8_P395_S001). Both companies state that dividends on these depositary shares are payable when and as declared by the Board.

comparisons.peer_topic: 2025 Issuance of Series Z Preferred Stock
comparisons.peer_summary: In January 2025, the firm issued 76,000 shares of Series Z 6.85% Fixed-Rate Reset Non-Cumulative Preferred Stock, which has a $25,000 liquidation preference, is redeemable at the firm's option starting February 10, 2030, and pays semi-annual dividends at 6.85% per annum until that date, thereafter resetting to 2.461% plus the five-year treasury rate.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi (Series DD) and Goldman Sachs (Series Z) disclose fixed-rate reset preferred stock structures where dividends are paid at a fixed rate until a specific reset date, after which the rate resets based on a benchmark treasury rate plus a spread. Citi's Series DD resets every 10 years to the 10-year treasury rate plus 2.757% (c_2024_8_P617_S002), while Goldman Sachs' Series Z resets to the five-year treasury rate plus 2.461% upon the redemption date in 2030 (gs_2024_8_P544_S003). Both specify that dividends are payable when declared.

sentences.text: Dividends are payable quarterly on February 15, May 15, August 15 and November 15 at a fixed rate until, but excluding, August 15, 2034, thereafter payable quarterly on the same dates at a fixed rate that resets on the Series DD reset date and every 10 years thereafter equal to the 10-year treasury rate plus 2.757%, in each case when, as and if declared by the Citi Board of Directors.

Dividends on Series Z Preferred Stock, if declared, are payable semi-annually at (i) 6.85% per annum from the issuance date to, but excluding, February 10, 2030 and, thereafter, (ii) 2.461% per annum plus the five-year treasury rate.

comparisons.peer_topic: Preferred Stock Dividend Policy and Reference Rates
comparisons.peer_summary: Dividends are discretionary, non-cumulative, and declared quarterly. Fixed-to-floating rate preferred stock uses SOFR or CMT as reference rates following the transition from LIBOR, with specific spread adjustments defined.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and JPMorgan describe the dividend mechanics of their fixed-to-floating preferred stock, noting that dividends are non-cumulative and payable only when declared. Citi’s Series DD pays quarterly fixed dividends until the reset date, after which the rate becomes floating based on the 10-year treasury rate (c_2024_8_P617_S002). JPMorgan explicitly states that fixed-to-floating rate preferred stock converts to a floating rate at the earliest redemption date and that dividends are payable semi-annually at the fixed rate and quarterly after conversion (jpm_2024_8_P748_S001, jpm_2024_8_P750_S004). While both use treasury-like benchmarks for resets, JPMorgan specifically notes the use of SOFR or CMT, whereas Citi uses the 10-year treasury rate for Series DD.

(b)Each series of fixed-to-floating rate preferred stock converts to a floating rate at the earliest redemption date.
Dividends are payable semiannually on fixed-to-floating rate preferred stock while at a fixed rate, and payable quarterly after converting to a floating rate.

comparisons.peer_summary: Series M preferred stock dividends are payable semiannually until September 15, 2026, and quarterly thereafter.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Morgan Stanley disclose preferred stock dividend payment frequency schedules that may change over time. Citi’s Series DD pays quarterly dividends from inception, with the *rate* resetting after 2034 (c_2024_8_P617_S002). In contrast, Morgan Stanley’s Series M specifies a change in *payment frequency*, being payable semiannually until September 15, 2026, and thereafter quarterly (ms_2024_8_P507_S001). Both disclosures address the temporal evolution of dividend terms for specific preferred series.
